First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 1) In first-order kinetics, elimination rate is:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: In first-order kinetics, elimination increases as plasma concentration increases. A constant fraction is eliminated per unit time. Most drugs follow first-order kinetics at therapeutic doses.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 2) In zero-order kinetics, elimination occurs as:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Zero-order kinetics means fixed amount is eliminated per unit time. Elimination is independent of plasma concentration. This occurs when elimination mechanisms are saturated.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 3) Half-life in first-order kinetics is usually:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: First-order kinetics has constant half-life. A constant fraction of drug is eliminated in each half-life. This makes dosing and elimination prediction easier.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 4) Half-life in zero-order kinetics is:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: In zero-order kinetics, half-life is not constant. A constant amount is removed per unit time. So the fraction removed changes with concentration.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 5) First-order kinetics means elimination of:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: First-order elimination removes a constant fraction of drug. The actual amount removed is larger when concentration is high. This is the usual pattern for most drugs.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 6) Zero-order kinetics means elimination of:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Zero-order elimination removes a fixed amount of drug per unit time. The pathway is usually saturated. Alcohol is a classic example.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 7) Low-dose aspirin is an example of:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Low-dose aspirin follows first-order kinetics. At lower concentrations, elimination mechanisms are not saturated. High-dose aspirin may show zero-order kinetics.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 8) High-dose aspirin is an example of:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: High-dose aspirin may show zero-order kinetics. At high concentration, elimination pathways become saturated. Then a constant amount is eliminated per unit time.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 9) Alcohol classically follows:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Alcohol is a classic zero-order drug. Its metabolism becomes saturated at usual intoxicating concentrations. Therefore a fixed amount is eliminated per unit time.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 10) Phenytoin is important because it may show:
First & Zero order kinetics,.option4: Saturable / zero-order kinetics at higher concentration
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Phenytoin can show saturable metabolism. Small dose increases may cause disproportionate plasma level rise. This is why monitoring is important.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 11) In zero-order kinetics, dose increase may cause:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Zero-order elimination becomes saturated. Extra dose cannot be cleared proportionally. So plasma concentration and toxicity risk may rise sharply.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 12) A drug eliminated by first-order kinetics will remove the same:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: First-order kinetics removes a constant fraction. For example, half of the remaining amount is removed each half-life. The absolute amount removed becomes smaller as concentration falls.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 13) A drug eliminated by zero-order kinetics will remove the same:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Zero-order kinetics removes a fixed amount over time. The percentage removed is not constant. This makes accumulation and toxicity more likely.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 14) Saturation of metabolizing enzymes is most closely related to:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Zero-order kinetics occurs when elimination capacity is saturated. Further concentration increase cannot proportionally increase elimination. This causes nonlinear kinetics.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 15) Therapeutic index is a measure of drug:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Therapeutic index measures drug safety. A higher therapeutic index means a wider safety margin. A low therapeutic index means close monitoring is needed.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 16) A higher therapeutic index indicates:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Higher therapeutic index means the toxic dose is much higher than the effective dose. Such drugs are safer in usual dosing. Lower therapeutic index drugs need careful monitoring.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 17) Which drug requires close monitoring due to low therapeutic index?
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Digoxin has a low therapeutic index. Small changes in plasma level may cause toxicity. Nausea, arrhythmia and visual disturbance are important warning features.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 18) Which drug is classically low therapeutic index?
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Warfarin has a narrow safety margin. Over-anticoagulation can cause bleeding. Monitoring of anticoagulant effect is important.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 19) Which drug commonly requires monitoring due to narrow safety margin?
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Lithium has a low therapeutic index. Toxicity can involve tremor, confusion, renal effects and seizures. Serum level monitoring is important.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 20) Aminoglycosides require monitoring mainly because of:
First & Zero order kinetics,.option2: Narrow safety margin and toxicity risk
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Aminoglycosides have important toxicity risk. Renal and ototoxic effects are major concerns. Therapeutic drug monitoring may be needed.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 21) Which anticancer drug is listed among low therapeutic index drugs?
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Methotrexate has a narrow safety margin. It can cause bone marrow, hepatic and mucosal toxicity. Monitoring is important during therapy.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 22) Which antiepileptic drug needs caution due to low therapeutic index?
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Phenytoin has narrow therapeutic range. It may show saturable metabolism. Small dose change can produce toxicity.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 23) Which drug has relatively high therapeutic index?
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Penicillin and many beta-lactams have relatively wide safety margin. They are safer than drugs like digoxin or lithium. Allergic reactions can still occur.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 24) Which drug is listed among wider safety margin drugs?
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Diazepam has a relatively wider therapeutic index. It is safer in usual therapeutic dosing than many narrow-index drugs. Clinical caution is still needed for sedation and dependence.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 25) Theophylline is clinically important because it has:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Theophylline has a narrow therapeutic range. Toxicity may include nausea, arrhythmia and seizures. Monitoring may be needed in selected patients.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 26) Half-life is the time required for plasma drug concentration to fall by:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Half-life means time needed for plasma concentration to fall by half. It helps determine dosing interval. It also predicts time to elimination and steady state.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 27) Half-life depends mainly on volume of distribution and:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Half-life depends mainly on volume of distribution and clearance. Higher Vd increases half-life. Higher clearance decreases half-life.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 28) Increased plasma protein binding usually:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Protein-bound drug acts as a storage form. It is released slowly. This tends to increase duration and half-life.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 29) High tissue binding or high Vd usually:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: High Vd means extensive tissue distribution. Drug returns slowly to plasma for elimination. This usually prolongs half-life.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 30) Increased metabolism usually:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Increased metabolism clears drug faster. This reduces plasma concentration more quickly. So half-life decreases.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 31) Increased renal clearance usually:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Increased renal clearance increases drug elimination. Faster elimination shortens half-life. Reduced clearance has the opposite effect.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 32) Kidney disease usually affects half-life by:
First & Zero order kinetics,.option3: Decreasing it due to faster excretion
First & Zero order kinetics,.option4: Increasing it due to reduced excretion
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Kidney disease reduces excretion of renally cleared drugs. This prolongs half-life. Dose adjustment may be needed to avoid toxicity.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 33) Liver disease usually increases half-life because of reduced:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Liver disease can reduce drug metabolism. Reduced metabolism prolongs half-life. This is important for hepatically metabolized drugs.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 34) A long half-life drug listed is:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Digoxin has a long half-life. It can accumulate if clearance is reduced. Monitoring and renal function assessment are important.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 35) Diazepam is classified as a:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Diazepam has long half-life. It may cause prolonged sedation, especially in vulnerable patients. Accumulation is possible with repeated dosing.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 36) Doxycycline is an example of:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Doxycycline is listed among long half-life drugs. Long half-life allows less frequent dosing. It may also prolong time to steady state.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 37) Adenosine is an example of:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Adenosine has very short half-life. Its action is brief. It is useful when rapid transient effect is desired.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 38) Which drug has short half-life?
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Lidocaine is listed among short half-life drugs. Short half-life drugs often require frequent dosing or infusion. They reach steady state faster than long half-life drugs.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 39) Which drug is short half-life?
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Dopamine has short half-life. It is usually administered by infusion when continuous effect is needed. The effect changes quickly when infusion is adjusted.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 40) Half-life helps determine:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Half-life helps determine dosing interval and frequency. It also predicts duration of action. It is important for drug accumulation.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 41) Steady state is reached when rate of drug administration equals rate of:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Steady state occurs when drug input equals drug elimination. Plasma concentration then remains relatively constant with regular dosing. It is important for maintenance therapy.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 42) Time to reach steady state depends mainly on:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Time to steady state depends on half-life. It does not become shorter simply by increasing dose. Long half-life drugs take longer to reach steady state.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 43) Approximately how many half-lives are needed to reach near steady state?
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: About 4–5 half-lives are required to reach 90–97% of steady state. The same principle applies to drug elimination after stopping. This is a key dosing concept.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 44) A drug with half-life of 24 hours reaches near steady state in about:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Near steady state requires 4–5 half-lives. For a 24-hour half-life, this equals about 4–5 days. Increasing dose does not shorten this time.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 45) A drug with half-life of 1 hour reaches near steady state in about:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Near steady state takes 4–5 half-lives. With half-life of 1 hour, this becomes 4–5 hours. Short half-life drugs reach steady state faster.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 46) Increasing maintenance dose will:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Increasing dose raises steady-state concentration. But it does not shorten time to true steady state. Time depends mainly on half-life.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 47) Loading dose is mainly used to:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Loading dose rapidly achieves target concentration. It is useful for long half-life drugs when delay is unacceptable. It does not change the drug’s actual half-life.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 48) A loading dose does:
First & Zero order kinetics,.option2: Reduce true steady-state time to zero
First & Zero order kinetics,.option3: Achieve target level quickly without shortening true steady-state time
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: Loading dose gives rapid therapeutic concentration. However, the underlying time to true steady state is still governed by half-life. Maintenance dose is needed to keep the level.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 49) After one half-life, the approximate amount of drug remaining is:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: After one half-life, half of the drug remains. After two half-lives, about 25% remains. This applies clearly to first-order elimination.

First & Zero order kinetics,.question: 50) After about five half-lives, approximate drug elimination is:
First & Zero order kinetics,.exp: After five half-lives, about 97% of drug is eliminated. Similarly, about 97% of steady state is reached after five half-lives. This rule is useful for predicting washout and accumulation.
